page: Microsoft Azure F64ams_v7 is a compute and memory-intensive virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is powered by dedicated x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processors operating at up to 4.5 GHz across 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading. It is configured with 512 GB of RAM, offering an 8 GB per vCPU allocation. Processor extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI. The instance does not include bundled local disk storage or integrated GPUs, relying entirely on attached remote network or premium storage volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark evaluations position this configuration in the top tier across compute and memory disciplines. Stress-ng single-core and multi-core results rank in the top 10 percent, matching the Passmark CPU score of 114,955.24. High-capacity memory bandwidth is verified by 398.73 GB/sec uncached read rates and 204.1 GB/sec write rates. Practical application benchmarks demonstrate high throughput, including 170.72 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks and top-tier CPU-driven execution on small to medium-sized LLM inference workloads, though prompt processing speeds decline to median levels for 70B parameter models.

From an architectural standpoint, the F64ams_v7 provides high resource density by pairing single-threaded dedicated cores with an elevated memory profile, eliminating hyperthread contention. The absence of integrated local NVMe storage requires careful storage architecture design to maintain throughput during disk-heavy operations. This server is suited for high-demand enterprise environments, including large in-memory databases, distributed data processing, real-time analytics engines, parallel compilation, and CPU-based inference workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure F64ams_v7 is a high-performance compute and memory-intensive instance built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 platform. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 64 dedicated physical cores running at 4.5 GHz with one thread per core, paired with 512 GB of system memory at an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. It lacks integrated GPUs and includes no local disk storage, necessitating remote premium storage for persistence. In synthetic and application testing, the instance exhibits top-tier multi-core compute capability, high uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 398 GB/sec, and strong execution in Redis caching alongside small to medium-model CPU inference. Compute performance remains highly consistent due to dedicated core allocations. The F64ams_v7 is engineered for compute-heavy, memory-intensive production workloads including in-memory datastores, distributed batch processing, simulation modeling, and large-scale enterprise services.
